summary: The note describes the first annual Fun Run or Walkathon in the Greenwood Meadows neighborhood, scheduled for 10 September 2023 and focused on participation over competition. It covers how organizer Marissa Clark and a volunteer committee planned the route, secured local business sponsorships, built inclusive activities for all ages, and arranged charity donations and post-run food. It also features quotes and stories from organizers, volunteers and participants.
one_line: Greenwood Meadows prepares its first annual inclusive Fun Run or Walkathon on 10 September 2023, backed by local businesses, volunteers and charities.
key_facts: Greenwood Meadows' first annual Fun Run or Walkathon is scheduled for 10 September 2023.
The event emphasizes participation over competition and aims to include young, elderly and everyone in between.
Marissa Clark, a local high school teacher and fitness enthusiast, first came up with the idea and leads the organizing committee.
Tom Bennett, owner of the cafe 'Bean There', is on the organizing team and believes the run could "spark a flame of unity and health consciousness in Greenwood Meadows."
The route is a scenic 5-kilometer circuit through the neighborhood's most picturesque streets, with a 2-kilometer option for a lighter endeavor.
Kyle Anderson, organizer and fitness coach, helped ensure the route is challenging for seasoned runners yet safe for families and casual walkers.
Local businesses, from gyms to family bakeries, contributed water bottles, snacks and financial support for logistics and safety.
Sarah Jennings, president of the local Chamber of Commerce, praised local businesses and residents coming together for collective health and happiness.
Inclusive activities include a 'toddler trot,' a 'seniors' stride,' and a 'furry friends' fleet' for dog owners.
A portion of the proceeds will go to local charities chosen by the participants; Grace Kim, head of the neighborhood association, is the charity coordination lead.
Nutritionist and volunteer organizer Emma Larson curated post-run food vendors offering items like oat bars and smoothies.
Mike Thompson, coordinator of volunteer services, called the volunteers "the beating heart of this run"; they help with registration and first-aid.
Hundreds have registered to run or walk, with many more expected to cheer from the sidelines.
Teenager Amit Patel rallied friends to run in support of his little sister, who was recently diagnosed with diabetes.
Sasha Rodriguez, captain of the high school cross country team, encourages peers to run or volunteer, and 75-year-old George Whitney plans to take 'the slow lane' but finish.
